text:
mike: Trying the Docker quickstart behind a Cloudflare tunnel and my first request is failing with 402 even though my workspace looks Active in the console. Using sample-docker v0.2 + SDK v1.4.0.

tara: Are you using a user key or a service account? Cloudflared can rewrite Host/Origin headers which trips our billing proxy.

mike: User key (UI -> API keys). If I curl the container IP it's 200, via the public tunnel it returns 402 with body: {"error":{"code":"workspace_payment_required","message":"ws_cedar must add billing"}}. SDK logs show it retried once and then surfaced a 502 to the app.

oscar: The SDK's retry logic treats 402 as non-retriable normally; curious it retried for you. Are you on the bundled docker image or local SDK?
mike: Using the bundled runtime in the sample image. Maybe the container proxies change headers.
support-bot: INF-501 filed: Cloudflare/other tunnel host header rewrite can cause billing origin mismatch and odd SDK retry interactions.

tara: Quick workaround: run cloudflared with `--origin-request-header Host=localhost:3000` or set `--disable-chunked-encoding` depending on your tunnel config so X-Forwarded-Host is preserved. Also try a service account token to rule out profile/session edge cases.
mike: Confirmed `--origin-request-header Host=localhost:3000` fixed it. First call now 200. I'll add a note to the Docker quickstart and open a tiny DX PR explaining the billing CTA + tunnel header tip. Thanks! :raised_hands:
